title: The City That Paid People to Breed Rats #shorts

lines.text: What happens when you pay people to kill rats? In nineteen oh two, Hanoi found out.
Rats were spreading plague, so the French offered one cent per rat. Just bring us the tail.
Hunters showed up with over twenty thousand tails in a single day.
Then inspectors spotted rats running around with no tails. People were cutting them off, and letting the rats go.
Others opened rat farms on the edge of town.
The French cancelled the bounty. The rats stayed.
So what happens when you pay people to kill rats? They breed them. And in nineteen oh six, the plague hit again.

sources: https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/hanoi-rat-massacre-1902 (1902; one cent per rat, tail as proof; peak day over 20,000 tails; tailless rats released; rat farms on outskirts; bounty scrapped; 1906 plague outbreak; based on historian Michael Vann's research)
https://madeinchinajournal.com/?p=21957 (interview with historian Michael G. Vann)

facts.bounty: one cent per rat, tail as proof
facts.peak: over 20,000 tails in one day (sources differ on the exact date, so no date is stated)
facts.gaming: tails cut off live rats then released; rat farms on the outskirts
facts.caveat: story rests largely on historian Michael Vann's research of colonial archives
